newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Wall Street helps Taiwan stocks to 7-yr peak close.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street helps Taiwan stocks to 7-yr peak close.

text.p: Taiwan share prices, flush with momentum from Wall Street's record rally overnight, zoomed past feeble resistance to close at a seven-year peak on Friday, brokers said.
The weighted index, gaining steadily through most of the session, closed 1.83 percent or 164.94 points higher at 9,192.57. The index has not closed higher since its 9,292.37 finish on April 30, 1990.
Turnover was relatively heavy at T$160.91 billion, but still far short of the T$200 billion-plus levels regularly attained by the market during a torrid June bull run.
Brokers said investors' confidence was sparked after the Dow Jones industrial average surged 1.29 percent on Wednesday to reach an all-time high of 7,895.81.
"The Dow Jones rise became contagious," said Joe Chiou, analyst for Taiwan Securities Investment.
"Market sentiment was already bullish, and it was merely looking for an excuse to rise further," Chiou said.
Brokers said a dramatic easing of Taiwan's recent money rate squeeze had helped stock the market with ample liquidity.
That enabled the benchmark index to punch through moderate technical resistance at 9,131.86 -- its previous 1997 intrasession high set on June 30.
Friday's session notched an intraday high 9,218.21 before easing slightly in the final minutes of trade.

The overnight interbank rate, which had surged into double digit in the final week of June, nosedived to 5.838 percent on Thursday from Wednesday's 9.813. It had rebounded to 6.481 percent by Friday's midday recess.
